newsitem.title: UK: ALUMINIUM TURNS DOWN ON LME, FILLS CHART GAP.
newsitem.headline: ALUMINIUM TURNS DOWN ON LME, FILLS CHART GAP.

text.p: Aluminium prices turned lower during early Friday LME trading, with the over-heated market staging a technical correction and filling a downside chart gap, traders said.
Other LME metals traded slowly, with little significant interest seen ahead of the weekend. Prices were on balance mixed.
"It has been a quiet morning so far. Apart from aluminium, nothing is really doing anything exciting," one trader said.
Aluminium business ranged from $1,753 down to $1,735 a tonne, filling the gap in the mid-$1,740s. Recent trade was at $1,735, down from Thursday's kerb close of $1,762.50.
"It has come back from $1,775 (Thursday's 22-month high) which is a $40 reaction...so it looks perfectly sound," another trader said.
Copper, meanwhile, was sagging as a 2,925-tonne stock rise was another in line with the consistent run of inventory increases.
Three months prices back-tracked to $2,312, down $21, with the market now seen testing the $2,310 upside break-out point from Thursday.
Traders said copper stalled at $2,340 - the upper level of a $2,270/2,340 band.
Zinc was holding at a steady $1,536/40 a tonne, while lead was similarly steady at $615/618.
Tin eased $20 to $5,620, while another 150-tonne stock increase pushed nickel some $80 lower to $7,160/90. Alloy was quiet at a slightly softer $1,535/40 a tonne.
